one_liner: Header-only unique-ownership smart pointer with observer_ptr; dereference is 3.5x-38.7x faster than std::weak_ptr::lock().
what_it_does: Provides observable_unique_ptr/observable_sealed_ptr as unique-ownership owners (like std::unique_ptr, movable not copyable) that can be watched by non-owning observer_ptr, filling the role std::weak_ptr fills for std::shared_ptr but without shared ownership. observer_ptr exposes expired(), operator*, operator-> similar to a locked weak_ptr, but there is no lock()/temporary-shared_ptr step. Not a drop-in for std::weak_ptr or std::shared_ptr: it is a different ownership model (unique, not shared), so call sites that rely on weak_ptr::lock() extending lifetime must be rewritten.
how_it_is_fast: The reference/expiry counter is a plain (non-atomic) integer in a small heap control block, so dereferencing an observer_ptr is just a flag check plus pointer read, versus std::weak_ptr::lock() which does an atomic increment, constructs a temporary shared_ptr, then an atomic decrement. Dropping shared ownership also shrinks the control block to 4 bytes (vs shared_ptr's ~24-byte block), cutting a heap allocation's worth of bookkeeping touched per access.
when_to_use: Object has one clear owner and you only need to detect "has this been destroyed yet", not extend its lifetime
Observer dereference/expiry-check happens in a hot loop and the object and its observers stay on a single thread
You want observer-pointer semantics without std::shared_ptr's control-block allocation and atomic refcount overhead
Header-only C++17 codebase where adding a single header is acceptable (no build system integration required)
Multiple inheritance with observer_from_this()-style self-observation (std::enable_shared_from_this doesn't support this)
when_not_to_use: Observer pointers or the owner must be touched from more than one thread — no synchronization on the refcount, unlike std::shared_ptr/weak_ptr
You need shared ownership (multiple owners) rather than unique ownership with observers
You need arrays (T[]) or custom allocator support — both unimplemented
Owner-pointer construction/creation is on the hot path — creating an oup owner is 1.1x-2.9x slower than std::unique_ptr/std::shared_ptr in the project's own benchmark table

You need observable_sealed_ptr with a custom deleter, or a default-constructible/copyable/movable T combined with enable_observer_from_this_sealed (that path requires T's constructor to accept a control block)

integration.min_toolchain: C++17 (CMakeLists.txt sets cxx_std_17; cmake_minimum_required 3.8+ if using the provided CMake target)
integration.platforms: any; CI builds Linux (GCC/clang), Windows (MSVC 32/64), macOS (clang), WebAssembly (Emscripten)
integration.thread_safety: Not thread-safe: refcount/control-block operations are unsynchronized. Unsafe for an owner on one thread to be observed from another thread. Safe in multithreaded programs as long as all observer_ptrs for a given object stay on that object's thread.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — explain: API shape (expired(), deref) mirrors std::weak_ptr's locked-use pattern, but the ownership model is unique not shared, so it replaces unique_ptr+weak_ptr-style usage, not shared_ptr+weak_ptr call sites verbatim.

gotchas: enable_observer_from_this_sealed requires T's constructor to accept a control block argument, which makes T non-default-constructible, non-copyable, and non-movable
enable_observer_from_this_unique uses virtual inheritance to support multiple inheritance, which has its own ABI/layout cost
observable_sealed_ptr does not support a custom deleter (observable_unique_ptr does)
observer_from_this() throws a documented exception type when called in situations where no valid control block exists yet (e.g., certain construction states)
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick oup over CDRC atomic_weak_ptr (concurrent_deferred_rc) when you have single-threaded or thread-confined ownership and want the smallest, simplest observer pointer; pick CDRC instead when observers must be read/written concurrently across threads, since oup has no synchronization at all. The std::function alternatives in this category (woid, Delegate, stdext::inplace_function, SmallFunction, sy_callback) solve a different problem (callable storage) and aren't a substitute for either.
verified_claims_summary: README's own speed_benchmark.cpp results (median across int/float/std::string/std::array<int,65536> objects, relative to raw T*=1) show observer_ptr dereference beating std::weak_ptr::lock()-based dereference by ~3.5x on gcc 9.4.0/libstdc++-9/Ryzen 5 2600, ~9.4x-11.8x on MSVC 16.11.3/MS-STL/i7-7800X, and ~38.7x on Emscripten 2.0.34/libc++ under Node.js 14.15.5/Ryzen 5 2600. The same tables show creating the owner pointer itself is 1.1x-2.9x slower than std::unique_ptr/std::shared_ptr, so the win is specific to the observer/dereference path, not owner construction.
status_note: Actively maintained (last commit 2026-09-05, project at v0.7.3 per CMakeLists.txt, MIT licensed), but the README states the speed benchmarks were last run for v0.7.1, so current numbers are unverified against the latest code. Small single-header library with no open issues; safe to vendor given the license and size.
